history.sg_progress: The Administration continues to engage with the permanent missions to the United Nations of unrepresented and underrepresented Member States to identify avenues to target their nationals for careers in the United Nations. Career briefings targeted to aspiring young nationals and mid-career professionals are being conducted. A model purposeful partnership agreement has also been pursued with selected Member States and proposals to identify activities for potential collaboration are being considered. In addition, the Administration has made efforts to build a database of online job boards that are used by nationals in underrepresented and unrepresented countries, with a three-tiered approach: job boards that are used on a national level, those that are used on a regional level and major global job boards. While the Office of Human Resources provides hiring offices with access to those boards, it has also started looking into automatized posting of jobs online by linking some of the boards to Inspira. The latter is a new project in its beginning phase but promises to yield a higher return on investment than manual postings. As part of its efforts, the Office has signed a memorandum of understanding with the networks of resident coordinators and United Nations information centres to leverage them in promoting the work of the United Nations and attracting talent from unrepresented and underrepresented Member States. The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure by the Board.

history.administration_response: The Office of Human Resources has implemented a number of initiatives to ensure job opportunities are sufficiently publicized and accessible to all underrepresented and unrepresented groups: One partnership agreement has been signed between the Office and an underrepresented Member State to have a targeted approach to identifying and recruiting qualified talent into the Organization. The United Nations Careers Portal serves as a key talent outreach tool that provides a comprehensive overview of all the employment opportunities within the United Nations Secretariat. The services of 2 regional job boards, one in the Middle East and one for the Caribbean, have been contracted as part of a pilot project to reach audiences in those regions on familiar platforms that will lead to more engagement of applicants. Under the long-term agreement with LinkedIn, the Office aims to leverage specialized content to enhance the United Nations Secretariat’s presence on this platform and attract talent from diverse backgrounds. As part of the long-term agreement, the Office will have the ability to promote job openings on LinkedIn, target candidates and directly invite them to apply. With regard to social media, the Office, through comprehensive research, identified Facebook as the primary social media platform used for job searches in developing countries, particularly among underrepresented and unrepresented Member States. Given the above continuing efforts, we consider the recommendation closed.

history.sg_progress: The Administration has implemented a number of initiatives to ensure that job opportunities are sufficiently publicized and accessible to all underrepresented and unrepresented groups: (a) As from May 2024, the Office of Human Resources has a LinkedIn Recruiter licence, and this tool is being used to promote General Job Openings, senior-level positions and hard-to-fill position within the Secretariat to talent from diverse backgrounds; (b) The Office of Human Resources continues to explore the use of paid social media campaign in order to better target applicants from unrepresented and underrepresented Members States. This will be piloted for the 2024 Young Professionals Programme social media campaign; (c) The Office of Human Resources is implementing purposeful partnerships with a number of Member States, which will provide a more targeted approach to identifying and attracting sources of talent using channels identified by Member States. Member States have more insights into their labour markets and what works more effectively in terms of promoting job opportunities in the United Nations. Such partnerships would also establish pipelines of talent, which will be ready to compete for future job opportunities when they are published. The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure by the Board.

history.administration_response: The Administration is requesting the closure of this recommendation. To accelerate progress, the Secretariat recently launched a “Purposeful partnerships” programme with unrepresented and underrepresented Member States. This initiative emphasizes intentional collaboration to build talent pipelines and increase the number of qualified candidates from these Member States. To date, two “Purposeful partnership” agreements have been signed, covering all developing Member States that are unrepresented or underrepresented. Further partnerships are under discussion. Given that this is an ongoing initiative, the Administration is requesting closure of the recommendation.
